run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: All three indices exist and were queried; each index uses a different severity/timestamp schema, so all three queries as literally requested returned 0 and had to be re-run against the actual mapped fields. Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps no `level` field (it uses `severity`, keyword); the re-run with `severity:"ERROR"` also returned 0, and no document in that index at all was matched inside the authorized window (match_all total 0, severity aggregation returned no buckets), even though the index holds 16 documents, so its ERROR total outside that window is unknown. Index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps no `level` field (it uses numeric `severity_num`); ERROR/FATAL there are severity_num 5 and 6, giving 8 documents (6 ERROR + 2 FATAL) inside the authorized window. Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps no `@timestamp` field (it uses `ingest_ts`, keyword); a keyword range over 2026-11-21 combined with `level:"ERROR"` returned 7 documents, while the whole index contains 16 documents of which 12 are level ERROR across both 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21. These are log-volume observations only: nothing here ties any of these documents to a service failure, and no incident cause is asserted.

claims.text: Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 is mapped with @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword); it has no `level` field, which is why `term: { level: "ERROR" }` matched nothing.
On app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 the query `term: { level: "ERROR" }` returned total 0 (relation eq) over the tool's 1-hour window 2026-11-21T05:56:21Z–2026-11-21T06:56:21Z.

On app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, a match_all query over the full authorized window 2026-11-20T06:56:21Z–2026-11-21T06:56:21Z returned total 0 and the terms aggregation on `severity` returned an empty bucket list, i.e. no document of that index fell inside the window.
The corrected re-run on app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, `term: { severity: "ERROR" }`, returned total 0 over the full authorized window 2026-11-20T06:56:21Z–2026-11-21T06:56:21Z.
At query time app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 held 16 documents (docs.count 16, 8.6kb), so the index is not empty even though no document matched inside the authorized window.

Index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 is mapped with @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); it has no `level` field, which is why `terms: { level: ["ERROR","FATAL"] }` returned total 0.
On app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 the only `severity_num` values present in the authorized window are 5 (6 docs), 3 (5 docs) and 6 (2 docs), total 13 documents (equal to the index docs.count 13).

In app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 the numeric severity maps as shown by the documents themselves: severity_num 5 = "[ERROR] DB timeout", severity_num 6 = "[FATAL] Disk full", severity_num 3 = "[INFO] healthcheck" (svc order-280).

The corrected query on app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, `terms: { severity_num: [5, 6] }` (ERROR + FATAL), returned total 8 over the authorized window 2026-11-20T06:56:21Z–2026-11-21T06:56:21Z, matching 6 severity_num=5 ERROR docs plus 2 severity_num=6 FATAL docs.

Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 is mapped with ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text); it maps no @timestamp field at all, which is why the @timestamp-range + level ERROR query returned total 0 and the tool noted that no matched index maps a date field, so no time filter was applied.

The corrected query on app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, keyword range ingest_ts gte 2026-11-21T00:00:00 lte 2026-11-21T23:59:59 AND level:"ERROR", returned total 7; the equivalent range gte "2026-11-21" lt "2026-11-22" also returned total 7.

app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 holds 16 documents in total: level buckets ERROR=12 and INFO=4, and ingest_ts buckets are one document each at 2026-11-20T08:01–08:05 (5 docs) and 2026-11-21T08:01–08:07 plus 09:01–09:04 (11 docs); the ingest_ts-only range for 2026-11-21 returned 11 documents.

app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3's 16 documents are unreachable through the mandatory @timestamp window filter because their @timestamp values (or the absence of that field in the documents) fall outside 2026-11-20T06:56:21Z–2026-11-21T06:56:21Z; the sibling index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 stores timestamps after the window end (2026-11-21T08:01–09:04), which is consistent with but does not prove this for index a. The index's real ERROR total is therefore undetermined.
The zero result for app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 is not explained by an empty or missing index: the index exists with health green, status open and docs.count 16.

For index a, count ERROR entries with the `severity` keyword field (not `level`) and widen the observation interval in the log platform itself; app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 cannot be counted outside 2026-11-20T06:56:21Z–2026-11-21T06:56:21Z through this tool because the @timestamp filter is fixed.

For index b use `severity_num` with the numeric codes seen in the documents (5=ERROR, 6=FATAL, 3=INFO); for index c use the keyword field `ingest_ts` with lexicographic range bounds such as gte "2026-11-21" / lt "2026-11-22", because `@timestamp` is not mapped there.

gaps: Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: the count of `severity:"ERROR"` documents outside 2026-11-20T06:56:21Z–2026-11-21T06:56:21Z is unknown. A match_all over that whole authorized window returned 0 even though docs.count is 16, and the tool's @timestamp filter cannot be turned off.

Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: it is unknown whether its 16 documents carry @timestamp values outside the window or carry no @timestamp field at all; no returned document from that index was ever seen, so its severity values are also unseen.

Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: whether the `level` field exists under a different name in the documents (e.g. severity value spelling such as "error" vs "ERROR") could not be verified, because no document from that index was retrievable inside the window.

Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3: ingest_ts is a keyword, not a date field, so "today" was applied as a lexicographic string range on 2026-11-21; timezone semantics of those strings are unknown, and the documents' timestamps (2026-11-21T08:01–09:04) lie after the authorized window end 2026-11-21T06:56:21Z, so they cannot be tied to the incident window.
No application, trace, Kubernetes or Prometheus evidence was examined for this request; the counts above are log-document counts only and do not establish service failures or affected entities.
next_steps: Map a date field (or a date-typed copy of ingest_ts) in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 so time-bounded queries and the tool's automatic time filter work, and confirm the intended timezone of the ingest_ts strings.
For app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, inspect the raw documents in Kibana or via _search to learn which field carries the event time, then correct the mapping so the index can be queried in a bounded window.
Confirm the numeric severity convention for app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 (5=ERROR, 6=FATAL, 3=INFO) and whether codes 1, 2 and 4 can occur, so ERROR/FATAL filters are complete.
If these log counts are meant to explain a service problem, follow up with per-service error-rate metrics and error spans for the named service rather than relying on document counts alone.
